sonnet.problem: The question says the waters are still covering the surface of all the earth. That rules out the wrong answers 'She stays out until the next morning' and 'She builds a nest in a tree', and it points straight to the right answer.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of a line ('be fruitful and multiply and ___ the earth'). The baker hasn't seen the word 'fill' and can't reason it out from the cards. 'Guard' and 'farm' are just other guesses at the wording.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answers 'seasonal' and 'temporary' mean nearly the same thing as each other. Both are the opposite of 'everlasting', which also makes the right answer stand out.
sonnet.rule: Two wrong answers never mean the same as each other either.
